name: Overhead Dumbbell Lunge
description: A lunge variation with dumbbells locked out overhead. The overhead position dramatically increases core stability demand, shoulder girdle endurance, and thoracic extension requirements while simultaneously training the lower body in a unilateral lunge pattern.

execution.starting_position: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand pressed overhead with elbows fully locked out and arms close to ears.
execution.setup_instructions: Press the dumbbells to lockout overhead before beginning. Confirm shoulder mobility allows a true vertical lockout position.
steps: Step 1: Take a large step forward with one foot and lower into a lunge, keeping dumbbells overhead throughout.
Step 2: Lower the rear knee toward the floor while keeping the torso upright and arms vertical.
Step 3: Drive through the front heel to step forward, bringing the feet together.
Step 4: Repeat on the opposite side, continuing to walk forward.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe steadily throughout. Do not hold your breath with heavy overhead loading.
common_mistakes: Allowing the arms to drift forward from vertical overhead
Hyperextending the lower back to compensate for limited shoulder mobility
safety_considerations: Use lighter dumbbells than you would for a standard lunge — the overhead position is very demanding
Lower the weights immediately if shoulder pain occurs
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full lunge depth (rear knee near floor, front thigh parallel). Arms remain fully extended overhead.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the armpits to keep arms vertical
Ribs down — do not flare them
